candidates.title: TrawMem: Reframing Agent Memory as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces
communitySignals: not found in HF Daily Papers batches checked
no Papers with Code reproduction repo
credibilityEvidence: Table 2/3: macro-F1 +2.23-3.14 vs 4 baselines (A-MEM/Mem0/LightMem/SimpleMem) on LoCoMo+MemGallery across 2 backbones
ablation on thread-expansion depth H (1-3) with time/quality tradeoff reported
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Consistent cross-backbone gains support the narrow claim (role-based retrieval beats relevance-only on these 2 conversational-memory benchmarks); no evidence on other agent task types
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Experiments are solid but scope is bounded to conversational-memory QA; no standalone Limitations section found in HTML render
candidates.primaryLimitation: No standalone Limitations section surfaced; validated only on LoCoMo/MemGallery conversational-memory benchmarks
candidates.presentationReason: Method, experiment tables (Table 1-3), and ablation are legible from the HTML render; conclusion/limitations section appears to be missing or merged elsewhere in the rendered HTML
candidates.reason: Reframes the basic retrieval question (relevance vs. task role) with cross-backbone, cross-baseline evidence; complements DiscernMem and EMMA at a different memory layer (single-agent retrieval vs. multi-agent correction vs. system-config)

candidates.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems
candidates.citationVelocity: published 3 days; Semantic Scholar API rate-limited (429) on retry, no data obtained this round
candidates.institution: East China Normal University + Ocean University of China + Tongji University + Information Engineering University
communitySignals: not found in HF Daily Papers batches checked
credibilityEvidence: Explicit Limitations section: paired-replay assumption, isolated per-rule evaluation blind spot, task-dependent benefit (binary-outcome QA makes effects neutral)
AutoGen/CAMEL/MacNet x 4 benchmarks, +0.51-4.32 pts over strongest baseline; CAMEL PDDL 37.71 vs 28.48
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Core claim supported on 3 frameworks x 4 benchmarks, but single 4B backbone only — no evidence of effect size at larger scale
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Clear methodology with disclosed limitations, but narrative strength bounded to the single small-backbone setting tested
candidates.primaryLimitation: Each memory evaluated/repaired in isolation; failures from multi-rule interaction cannot be fixed by editing a single rule
candidates.presentationReason: Method (DMR + BLM), experiments, and limitations are clearly delineated in the text
candidates.reason: Directly complements TrawMem by addressing memory correction rather than retrieval; has the most complete reproducibility artifact (public repo) of the three selected

candidates.title: EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis
candidates.citationVelocity: published 5 days; Semantic Scholar API rate-limited (429) on retry, no data obtained this round
communitySignals: not found in HF Daily Papers batches checked
no public code found for EMMA itself (references existing frameworks like smolagents, but core implementation not open-sourced)
credibilityEvidence: Explicit 'Conclusion and Limitations' section acknowledging unresolved cross-backbone-family gap and persisting ineffective edits

candidates.presentationReason: Explicit Conclusion and Limitations section, clear benchmark/baseline/backbone matrix
candidates.reason: Strongest evidence base of the three; adds a third memory layer (system-configuration-as-memory) distinct from TrawMem (retrieval) and DiscernMem (correction), directly challenging 4 widely-cited self-improvement baselines
